sights.w: The Redemptorist church that gave Novena its name — and its MRT station: built 1950 to a Swan & Maclaren design, eclectic-Modern with a triple-arched front pediment and circular stained-glass window, conserved in 2011, with a Gothic-style worship hall added in 2017. Its Saturday Perpetual Novena to Our Mother of Perpetual Help draws worshippers of every faith.
sights.k: Catholic church; Saturday novena services are its busiest hours

sights.w: A turreted, Rhineland-castle-style clubhouse built in 1900 as the Deutsches Haus of the German Teutonia Club, confiscated in WWI, bought in 1918 by the Manasseh brothers as Goodwood Hall and opened as a hotel in 1929 — gazetted the 22nd National Monument (1989). Its café is the city's famous durian-dessert address.
sights.k: National Monument; working hotel — the Tower Wing is viewable from the grounds

sights.w: Singapore's first permanent police training institution, opened 1929 off Thomson Road and in use for more than eight decades until the move to the Home Team Academy in 2005; its colonial-era buildings are conserved by URA as the heritage core of the coming Mount Pleasant housing estate.
sights.k: Conserved complex — view from Mount Pleasant Road; grounds under redevelopment

sights.n: Tan Tock Seng Hospital Heritage Museum
sights.address: Tan Tock Seng Hospital, 11 Jalan Tan Tock Seng, Singapore 308433
sights.w: Opened 2001 inside Singapore's first privately funded hospital (founded 1844 by philanthropist Tan Tock Seng 'for the sick poor of all nations'): artefacts, old medical equipment and a time capsule trace its fights against tuberculosis in the 1940s and SARS in 2003.
sights.k: Small free museum inside the hospital

sights.w: WOHA's first high-rise (2003), which re-imagined the curtain wall as a climate device — 'monsoon windows' adapted from Borneo longhouse bamboo vents let the flats ventilate even in the rain; it won the 2007 Aga Khan Award for Architecture.
sights.k: Private residential tower — view from outside

sights.w: Founded 1886 and at the corner of Mount Pleasant and Thomson Roads since 1941 — 27 acres of polo pitches and stables, one of Singapore's oldest sporting clubs; spectators come for its tournament seasons.
sights.k: Private club; open to the public on tournament days
